I have my side-effect concepts. Now let me run the main cross-tab: for SSRI patients, infer indication group, and count side effects occurring after SSRI start. I'll capture common indication groups (depression, anxiety disorders, OCD, panic, PTSD) via condition concept descendants, then join to side-effect conditions dated after the first SSRI exposure.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH ssri_drugs AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ca.descendant_concept_id AS drug_concept_id
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (797617,715939,755695,751412,722031,739138,40234834,44507700)
),
ssri_start AS (
  SELECT de.person_id, MIN(de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS first_ssri
  FROM omop.drug_exposure de
  JOIN ssri_drugs d ON de.drug_concept_id = d.drug_concept_id
  GROUP BY de.person_id
),
indication AS (
  SELECT s.person_id,
    CASE
      WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM omop.condition_occurrence co JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON co.condition_concept_id=ca.descendant_concept_id
                   WHERE co.person_id=s.person_id AND ca.ancestor_concept_id=440383) THEN 'Depression'
      WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM omop.condition_occurrence co JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON co.condition_concept_id=ca.descendant_concept_id
                   WHERE co.person_id=s.person_id AND ca.ancestor_concept_id=442077) THEN 'Anxiety disorder'
      WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM omop.condition_occurrence co JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON co.condition_concept_id=ca.descendant_concept_id
                   WHERE co.person_id=s.person_id AND ca.ancestor_concept_id=436676) THEN 'OCD'
      WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM omop.condition_occurrence co JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON co.condition_concept_id=ca.descendant_concept_id
                   WHERE co.person_id=s.person_id AND ca.ancestor_concept_id=436675) THEN 'PTSD'
      ELSE 'Other/Unspecified'
    END AS indication
  FROM ssri_start s
)
SELECT indication, COUNT(*) AS n_patients
FROM indication
GROUP BY indication
ORDER BY n_patients DESC;

content.text: The correlated-subquery approach is too slow at this scale. Let me pre-aggregate each patient's indication into a single joinable table using JOINs instead of `EXISTS`, and narrow the work. I'll compute indication flags per patient first, and keep it lean.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH ssri_pt AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT de.person_id
  FROM omop.drug_exposure de
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON de.drug_concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (797617,715939,755695,751412,722031,739138,40234834,44507700)
),
pt_ind AS (
  SELECT p.person_id,
         MAX(CASE WHEN ca.ancestor_concept_id=440383 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dep,
         MAX(CASE WHEN ca.ancestor_concept_id=442077 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS anx,
         MAX(CASE WHEN ca.ancestor_concept_id=436676 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS ocd,
         MAX(CASE WHEN ca.ancestor_concept_id=436675 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS ptsd
  FROM ssri_pt p
  JOIN omop.condition_occurrence co ON co.person_id=p.person_id
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON co.condition_concept_id=ca.descendant_concept_id
   AND ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (440383,442077,436676,436675)
  GROUP BY p.person_id
)
SELECT
  CASE WHEN dep=1 THEN 'Depression'
       WHEN anx=1 THEN 'Anxiety disorder'
       WHEN ocd=1 THEN 'OCD'
       WHEN ptsd=1 THEN 'PTSD' END AS indication,
  COUNT(*) AS n_patients
FROM pt_ind
GROUP BY CASE WHEN dep=1 THEN 'Depression'
       WHEN anx=1 THEN 'Anxiety disorder'
       WHEN ocd=1 THEN 'OCD'
       WHEN ptsd=1 THEN 'PTSD' END
ORDER BY n_patients DESC;

The indication cross-tab works (Depression 62,178; Anxiety 11,773; OCD 0 shown/very few; PTSD 412). Now the key step: count each side-effect condition, occurring **after** SSRI start, stratified by indication. I'll materialize a per-patient indication label and join to side-effect conditions.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH ssri_start AS (
  SELECT de.person_id, MIN(de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS first_ssri
  FROM omop.drug_exposure de
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON de.drug_concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (797617,715939,755695,751412,722031,739138,40234834,44507700)
  GROUP BY de.person_id
),
pt_ind AS (
  SELECT s.person_id, s.first_ssri,
         MAX(CASE WHEN ca.ancestor_concept_id=440383 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dep,
         MAX(CASE WHEN ca.ancestor_concept_id=442077 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS anx,
         MAX(CASE WHEN ca.ancestor_concept_id=436675 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS ptsd
  FROM ssri_start s
  JOIN omop.condition_occurrence co ON co.person_id=s.person_id
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON co.condition_concept_id=ca.descendant_concept_id
   AND ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (440383,442077,436675)
  GROUP BY s.person_id, s.first_ssri
),
labeled AS (
  SELECT person_id, first_ssri,
    CASE WHEN dep=1 THEN 'Depression' WHEN anx=1 THEN 'Anxiety disorder'
         WHEN ptsd=1 THEN 'PTSD' END AS indication
  FROM pt_ind
),
se AS (
  SELECT co.person_id, co.condition_concept_id, MIN(co.condition_start_date) AS se_date
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
  WHERE co.condition_concept_id IN (31967,27674,441408,196523,75860,378253,4223938,436962,443782,138565,4232311,4226991,4012381,441542,4099943,3655355)
  GROUP BY co.person_id, co.condition_concept_id
)
SELECT l.indication, c.concept_name AS side_effect,
       COUNT(DISTINCT se.person_id) AS n_patients
FROM labeled l
JOIN se ON se.person_id = l.person_id AND se.se_date >= l.first_ssri
JOIN omop.concept c ON c.concept_id = se.condition_concept_id
GROUP BY l.indication, c.concept_name
ORDER BY l.indication, n_patients DESC;

arguments.title: SSRI-associated side effects across treatment indications
arguments.subtitle: OMOP cohort: 105,836 SSRI-exposed patients; side effects recorded on/after first SSRI dispense
arguments.summary:
This report ranks common SSRI-associated side effects among SSRI-treated patients, stratified by inferred treatment indication (Depression n=62,178; Anxiety disorder n=11,773; PTSD n=412). Indication was inferred from each patient's condition history; a patient with depression takes precedence over anxiety/PTSD, so groups are mutually exclusive. Side effects were counted only when the condition was first recorded on or after the patient's first SSRI exposure.

Key findings:
- **Gastrointestinal (nausea, diarrhea, constipation) and neurologic (headache, insomnia, dizziness) complaints are the most common side effects in every indication.**
- **Insomnia and headache are relatively more prominent in Depression, while nausea/constipation dominate in the small PTSD group.**
- The 'Anxiety' side-effect row overlaps conceptually with the anxiety indication and should be interpreted cautiously.
- PTSD (n=412) is too small for stable rate estimates and is shown for completeness only.

sections.title: Rates within each indication
sections.description: Percentage of that indication's SSRI patients who had each side effect recorded after starting an SSRI. Rates control for the very different group sizes.

panels.title: Top side effects by indication (% of patients)
panels.caption: GI and neurologic symptoms lead across all groups. **Anxiety disorder** patients show the highest 'anxiety' rate (27.7%); **Depression** patients have notably higher insomnia (13.0%) and headache (10.7%).
panels.notes: Denominators: Depression 62,178; Anxiety 11,773; PTSD 412. Side effect = SNOMED condition concept first recorded on/after first SSRI exposure date. Indications inferred from condition history, mutually exclusive with precedence Depression > Anxiety > PTSD.

sections.title: Absolute patient counts
sections.description: The same side effects as raw patient counts, dominated by the large Depression group.

panels.title: Patient counts by side effect and indication
panels.caption: Anxiety, insomnia, constipation, headache, nausea and diarrhea are the highest-volume side effects, driven mainly by the Depression cohort.

arguments.footer: Method notes & caveats: SSRIs identified as descendants of the ingredients citalopram, escitalopram, fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, paroxetine, sertraline, vilazodone, vortioxetine. Side effects are condition records temporally after SSRI start — this is co-occurrence, not a proven drug-attributed adverse reaction (no causal/attribution field exists in this OMOP data, and pre-existing symptoms such as insomnia or anxiety may reflect the underlying disorder rather than the drug). OCD yielded too few labeled patients to report. Rates are within-indication and not adjusted for follow-up time, comorbidity, or dose.

Findings are in the report in the side panel. Summary:

**Most common SSRI side effects are GI + neurologic, consistently across indications.** In every group the top recorded side effects are constipation, nausea, diarrhea, headache, insomnia, and dizziness.

By indication (% of that indication's SSRI patients, side effect recorded on/after first SSRI dispense):

- **Depression (n=62,178):** insomnia 13.0%, constipation 11.6%, headache 10.7%, nausea 9.6%, diarrhea 9.3% — insomnia and headache stand out here.
- **Anxiety disorder (n=11,773):** insomnia 8.7%, constipation 7.4%, headache 6.8%, nausea 6.1%, diarrhea 6.1% — same rank order, lower rates.
- **PTSD (n=412):** constipation 17.7%, nausea 14.1% lead, but n is too small for stable estimates.

Important caveats:
- These are **temporal co-occurrences**, not attributed adverse reactions — this OMOP data has no causality field, and symptoms like insomnia/anxiety may reflect the underlying disorder rather than the drug.
- Indication was **inferred** from condition history (mutually exclusive, precedence Depression > Anxiety > PTSD); the "Anxiety" side-effect row overlaps the anxiety indication.
- Rates aren't adjusted for follow-up time, dose, or comorbidity.
